THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 17, 1926

Correspondence

THE CHINA PRESS welcomes the views of its readers on subjects of the day, but publication in the correspondence column does not mean necessarily that the views expressed by correspondents are those of THE CHINA PRESS. Manuscripts submitted for this department should be plainly written on one side of the paper only and should be type-written if possible. No letters will be returned to writers unless requested and accompanied by self-addressed and stamped envelope. Communications should not exceed more than 400 words in length.

THE LAWYERS AND THE MIXED COURT.
Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Dear Sir:—It is with an ever deepening interest that I read during the past few days your reports of the actions taken by the foreign legal fraternity of Shanghai to oppose the rendition of the Mixed Court to Chinese control and administration, especially the report that a meeting, participated in by the legal lights of different nationalities, which commenced by spectacularly ousting the journalists coming on their own invitation, ended by adopting a publicity campaign. The Memorandum of the Far Eastern American Bar Association which you publish in today's paper seems one of the forms in which the "campaign" finds expression. Instead of merely launching opposition to the reported Mixed Court Agreement, the Bar Association has seen fit to offer in the Memorandum some concrete measures in the form of recommendations in order to safeguard the reforms and improvements effected since the Court came to the hands of the Consular Body. The interest which the American Bar Association takes in the welfare of the Shanghai community as secured and guaranteed by the efficient administration of justice must be appreciated by the Chinese no less than the foreign public, despite the prevalent opinion that all the actions on the part of the foreign legal fraternity in this regard are prompted by the sordid desire to maintain its foothold in a locality where legal practice proves to be exceedingly lucrative.

A reading of the Memorandum in its entirety, however, reveals that besides the arguments advanced by the American Bar which are hardly convincing, there are not a few places where the inaccurate statements of facts and incorrect views are likely to mislead the public. It is in refutation of these statements and views that the present letter is written.

The Memorandum opens with an account of the Mixed Court before 1911 and an enumeration of the "abuses" at that time. Then follows a similar enumeration of the "advantages" which have accrued since the Consular Body assumed the control of the Court. It seems to the American Bar that as soon as the Court is handed back to China, "a revival of the old abuses, corruptions, bribery, and chicanery" will be the result. It is true that some of the abuses enumerated did exist in the Court before 1911, yet can one deny that many of these very abuses still enjoy a continued existence, perhaps in different forms, in the Mixed Court as it is at present? To make the matter worse, the Court since 1911 has been responsible for causing certain other abuses and inconveniences which were wholly unknown and unimaginable before 1911. Instead of adopting the method of enumeration at length which will not be allowed by space, suffice it to mention three points:

(1) The uncertain state of the law the Court applies. Nominally the Court claims to apply Chinese law. But in practice, even from the point of view of the casual observer, it is interesting to see in open court the foreign lawyers base their contentions on foreign laws and submit authorities from foreign codes, which are wholly unknown to the litigants. The complex and indeterminate mass of laws now applied by the Court can scarcely ensure a feeling of security to the residents of the Settlement who are at a loss to know which way to turn amid the maze of uncertain laws and often conflicting decisions.

(2) It is a notorious scandal in the Settlement that most lawyers practising now in the Mixed Court get their clients through brokers, who spare no pains to fan up the flame of controversies in order that they may bring business to their lawyers. Such practice is unprecedented among lawyers in foreign countries and there has never been a code of legal ethics which tolerates such improper manner of getting clients. Yet the Mixed Court apparently connives at the misconduct of the members of its bar. This partly accounts for the abundance of suits in the Court and also for the much cited saying that Chinese litigants are more ready to bring suits in the Mixed Court than in the native court.

(3) The extremely high rate of the court costs makes it often beyond the power of an average Chinese to institute a legal proceeding. Besides, owing to the important position the foreign lawyers occupy in the Court, many Chinese litigants are compelled to retain them at very high fees. Those who can ill afford to do so are thus debarred from getting what little justice the Court has to offer, for even that little justice can only be dearly bought.

What we wish to be accomplished in connection with the contemplated rendition is not only the elimination of the abuses existing prior to 1911 but also the elimination of the abuses and inconveniences found at the present time. It is a bold statement to say that the old abuses will revive when the Court is handed back to the Chinese. Besides, such statement is calculated to belittle and perhaps to prevent the honest and painstaking efforts put forth by the negotiating parties to devise ways and means to improve the Mixed Court as it is.

One phase of the Mixed Court Procedure which meets the special approval of the American legal fraternity is the system of examination and cross-examination of witnesses by counsel. The absence of such a procedure seems to the authors of the Memorandum to be a hindrance to the administration of justice. The Chinese procedure is criticized because it provides that the judge may independently make investigations. Such arguments show nothing more than the fact that the American legal fraternity is a staunch supporter of the Anglo-American system of procedure and the further fact that other systems of procedure now in force in other leading countries are apparently unknown to the jurisconsults of the American Bar at Shanghai. It is a rule in the French Code of Procedure that "le juge peut recourir à des constatations matérielles, soit par lui-même, au moyen d'une descente sur les lieux..." (see Art. 295, Code de Procedure

《字林西报》，1926年7月17日，星期六

读者来信

《字林西报》欢迎读者就当日时事发表观点，但刊登在读者来信栏目的文章并不必然代表《字林西报》的立场。投寄至本栏目的稿件应仅写在纸张的一面，字迹清晰，如可能请以打字机打印。除非作者要求并附具写好回信地址且贴足邮票的信封，否则信件概不退还。通讯篇幅不得超过 400 字。

律师与会审公廨。
致《字林西报》编辑：
尊敬的先生：——在过去几天里，我怀着日益浓厚的兴趣阅读了贵报关于上海外国法律界反对将会审公廨移交中国控制和管理所采取行动的报道，特别是那篇报道指出，一场由各国法律界名流参加的会议，以戏剧性地驱逐自行前来的记者开场，最终以通过一项宣传运动告终。贵报今日刊登的《远东美国律师协会备忘录》似乎是该“运动”的表现形式之一。该律师协会并未仅仅对传闻中的《会审公廨协定》表示反对，而是认为应当在备忘录中以建议的形式提出一些具体措施，以 safeguard（保卫）自该法庭落入领事团手中以来所实施的改革和改进。尽管普遍存在一种观点，认为外国法律界在此方面的所有行动都是出于维持其在法律执业利润极其丰厚之地立足点的卑劣欲望，但中美公众同样必须认可美国律师协会对上海社区福祉的关注，这种福祉是通过高效的司法行政得以保障和确保的。

然而，通读整份备忘录后发现，除了美国律师提出的那些难以令人信服的论点外，还有不少地方存在不实的事实陈述和错误的观点，可能会误导公众。本信正是为了驳斥这些陈述和观点而写。

备忘录开篇叙述了 1911 年以前的会审公廨情况，并列举了当时的种种“弊端”。随后，又类似地列举了自领事团接管法庭以来所产生的“优势”。在美国律师看来，一旦将法庭交还中国，结果将是“旧有的弊端、腐败、贿赂和欺诈手段死灰复燃”。诚然，所列举的部分弊端在 1911 年以前的法庭中确实存在，但能否否认，其中许多弊端至今仍以不同的形式在目前的会审公廨中继续存在？更糟糕的是，自 1911 年以来，该法庭还导致了一些在 1911 年之前完全未知且无法想象的其他弊端和不便。鉴于篇幅限制，无法采用详细列举的方法，此处仅提及三点：

(1) 法庭适用法律的状态不确定。名义上，法庭声称适用中国法律。但在实践中，即使是旁观者也不难发现，外国律师在公开庭审中依据外国法律进行辩论，并提交当事人完全陌生的外国法典作为权威依据。法庭目前适用的庞大、复杂且不确定的法律体系，几乎无法让租界居民产生安全感，他们在不确定的法律迷宫和经常相互冲突的判决中不知所措。

(2) 目前在会审公廨执业的大多数律师通过掮客获取客户，这在租界已是众所周知的丑闻；这些掮客不遗余力地煽动争议火焰，以便为他们的律师带来业务。这种做法在外国律师中是前所未有的，没有任何法律职业道德规范容忍这种不当的客户招揽方式。然而，会审公廨显然对其律师团成员的不当行为视而不见。这部分解释了法庭诉讼案件众多的原因，也解释了那句常被引用的说法，即中国诉讼人更愿意在会审公廨而非中国本土法庭提起诉讼。

(3) 极高的诉讼费用往往使普通中国人无力提起法律诉讼。此外，由于外国律师在法庭中占据重要地位，许多中国诉讼人被迫以高昂的费用聘请他们。那些无力承担此费用的人因此被剥夺了获得法庭所能提供的少许正义的机会，因为即便是这少许正义，也只能以昂贵的代价换取。

我们就拟议中的移交工作希望达成的目标，不仅是消除 1911 年之前存在的弊端，还要消除当前发现的弊端和不便。断言法庭交还中国后旧弊将死灰复燃，这是一种大胆的说法。此外，这种说法旨在贬低，甚至可能阻碍谈判各方为改善现有会审公廨状况而付出的诚实且艰辛的努力，他们正在 devising（谋划）各种方法和手段。

会审公廨程序中获得美国法律界特别认可的一个方面是由 counsel（辩护律师）对证人进行讯问和交叉讯问的制度。备忘录的作者认为，缺乏此类程序妨碍了司法公正。中国程序受到批评，是因为它规定法官可以独立进行调查。此类论点仅表明美国法律界是英美法系程序的坚定支持者，同时也表明上海美国律师协会的法学家们显然不了解其他主要国家目前施行的其他程序制度。《法国民事诉讼法典》规定：“法官可以亲自或通过现场勘验等方式进行事实认定……”（参见《民事诉讼法典》第 295 条

Civile). The German Procedural Code contains a special chapter consisting of 25 articles on the investigation of evidence independently by the judge or the judges. A chapter, too, is devoted in the Japanese Code of Civil Procedure on the independent investigation of the Court. Right here, attention should be called to the incorrect statement of the Memorandum, saying that "Chinese judges may, on their own initiative, secretly, investigate the evidence." The use of the word "secretly" is without foundation, for nowhere is this word found in the articles of Code of Procedure nor can it be implied therein. In all cases of civil nature, investigations are open or the data upon which the investigations are based must be stated. The opinion of the American Bar seems to be that justice cannot be done unless the method of cross-examination, a peculiar product of their own legal institutions, is adopted. Looking the matter from another angle, we might say that the citizens of the French, German, Japanese, or other nations where this system is unknown, may launch similar objection to the adoption of the same with all its disadvantages, among which may be mentioned the bullying of the witnesses by the lawyer, a frequent occurrence in the Mixed Court.

It is an extremely deplorable fact that many of the writers on Chinese affairs, especially on Chinese judicial conditions, generalize, or induce others to generalize, on the basis of a few isolated instances wishing to attack the Chinese judiciary, the American Bar in the Memorandum cites triumphantly the instances where the late Magistrate of the Mixed Court, before the Revolution absconded with a sum of money and where, judge Mei Yi-kuo of the Shanghai District Court committed the same offence. Unless the authors of the Memorandum can prove that absconding is the general rule, instead of the exception, among Chinese judges, the two instances cited furnish no basis for jumping to the conclusion that funds are not safe in the hands of Chinese courts. Perhaps at the time of writing the Memorandum, the drafting committee of the American Bar did not yet have knowledge of the fact that the Clerk of the very Court of which the lawyers are the officers, is alleged to have absconded with court funds amounting to from $30,000 to $100,000. They also seem to have forgotten that another Clerk of the U. S. Court and later a member of a prominent firm, Mr. Earl B. Rose, also fled from Shanghai after being accused of embezzlement and that in the fall of last year a prominent member of the American Bar disappeared from Shanghai in order to avoid a charge of arms-dealing. From these instances of defalcations of some individual offenders, no sensible man will jump to the conclusion that all the Clerks of the U. S. Court are likely to embezzle and therefore it is unsafe to deposit funds there, and that it is not prudent to trust the American lawyers with cases because some of them do not possess as high a moral character as is demanded by the profession. Similarly, to cite the remarks of Judge Tu in the Shanghai District Court does not induce the conclusion that the proposition announced represents the rule of Chinese law, when we bear in mind that strange doctrines are found very often in the cases reported in American or English reports, which cases are, of course, reversed by more mature juridical minds.

The participation of a foreign judge in the decision of cases, as recommended by the Memorandum, is an important issue. The Memorandum seeks to justify this recommendation on the ground that most of the laws of China are modelled after those of Western countries and Chinese judges cannot be expected to administer Western conceptions of law without guidance. This recommendation has to be declined with thanks, because the modern Chinese laws are not a wholesale reproduction of Western laws but have been adapted in view of particular Chinese conditions. No jurist of any particular country can help Chinese judges in this regard, because there exists as much difference among the various conceptions of Western laws as followed in different countries as between any Western conception and the Chinese conception of law. Only Chinese jurists who have mastered both the Western systems of law and the old Chinese system can make adjustments between the new and old conceptions. As to the disadvantages of the dual judge system in the Mixed Court suffice it to quote the words of Mr. Latter, a British barrister, one time of the Bar of the Mixed Court, in the "Law Quarterly Review:"

"Too often do the proceedings in this Court (the Mixed Court), develop into a mere wrangle between the assessor and magistrate, each advocating the cause of his own sovereign subject. Sometimes the Court adjourns in high disagreement. At other times, weary of its civil strife, it tosses the ball back to the litigants and bids them see to it themselves........

The Memorandum also eulogizes the part played by Western lawyers in maintaining the standard of the Court. With all deference to the integrity and ability of these lawyers, one cannot deny that in purely civil cases much time is wasted and much inconvenience is caused by the presence of these lawyers speaking different languages, advocating different systems of laws, and charging unregulated fees. The scandalous practice of soliciting business through brokers has been referred to. The writer does not propose to discuss about their exclusion after the rendition of the Court, inasmuch as those charged with the task will see their way to make an arrangement. But one thing has to be noted. The Mixed Court, acting on the instructions of the Consular Body, has been very lax in admitting persons to the Bar. Definite qualifications are required by our Regulations for Lawyers in order to be admitted to the Chinese Bar. But it not infrequently happens that persons falling far short of these qualifications are admitted to practice in the Mixed Court on the recommendation of one or two attorneys. These persons are often mere interpreters of foreign lawyers and scarcely possess a liberal education, to say nothing of legal knowledge. In order to raise the standards, both moral and intellectual, of the Mixed Court Bar, it behooves the authorities to see to it hereafter that no person is admitted who cannot qualify under the Regulations promulgated by the Ministry of Justice for Lawyers.

In conclusion, the writer ventures the hope that those charged with the grave task of negotiating over the Mixed Court will be so conscious of their responsibility as not to be influenced by the "public campaigns," but will also listen to such counsels as are consistent with the desire for public welfare.

Thanking you for your space.
I am, etc.,
LIANG YUENG-LI
Shanghai, July 15, 1926.

民事）。《德国民事诉讼法》设有一章，共二十五条，专门规定法官独立调查证据。日本《民事诉讼法》中也有一章专门规定法院的独立调查。在此必须指出，备忘录中称“中国法官可以主动秘密调查证据”，这一说法是不正确的。“秘密”一词毫无根据，因为在诉讼法条文中既找不到这个词，也无法从中推断出这层含义。在所有民事案件中，调查都是公开的，或者必须说明调查所依据的材料。美国律师界的观点似乎是，除非采用其自身法律制度特有的交叉询问方法，否则无法实现司法公正。从另一个角度来看，我们可以说，法国、德国、日本或其他不熟悉该制度的国家的公民，可能会对该制度及其所有弊端提出类似的反对意见，其中包括律师对证人的欺凌，这在会审公廨中是经常发生的。

令人极为痛心的是，许多撰写中国事务、特别是中国司法状况的作者，往往基于个别孤立案例进行概括，或诱导他人进行概括，以此攻击中国司法界；美国律师界在备忘录中得意地引用了以下案例：革命前，会审公廨的前任谳员携款潜逃，以及上海地方法院法官梅贻谷犯下同样的罪行。除非备忘录的作者能够证明，携款潜逃是中国法官中的普遍现象而非例外，否则所引用的这两个案例并不能成为得出“资金在中国法院手中不安全”这一结论的依据。也许在起草备忘录时，美国律师界的起草委员会尚不知晓这样一个事实：据称，就在这些律师作为职员的同一法院，其书记员已携法院资金潜逃，金额达三万至十万美元。他们似乎还忘记了，美国法院的另一名书记员、后来是一家著名律师事务所成员的厄尔·B·罗斯（Earl B. Rose）先生，在被指控挪用公款后也逃离了上海；而且去年秋天，美国律师界的一位知名成员为逃避军火交易指控而从上海失踪。从这些个别违法者的贪污案例中，任何理智的人都不会贸然得出这样的结论：美国法院的所有书记员都可能挪用公款，因此在那里存款是不安全的；也不会因为某些美国律师不具备该职业所要求的高尚道德品质，就认为将案件委托给美国律师是不明智的。同样，引用上海地方法院杜法官的言论，并不能使人得出其所宣布的主张代表中国法律规则的结论，因为我们应当记得，在美国或英国的判例报告中，经常可以发现奇怪的学说，而这些案件当然会被更成熟的司法头脑所推翻。

备忘录建议外国法官参与案件裁决，这是一个重要问题。备忘录试图以中国大多数法律均仿效西方国家法律、且若无指导则不能期望中国法官实施西方法律观念为由，为这一建议辩护。这一建议必须婉言谢绝，因为现代中国法律并非对西方法律的全盘复制，而是根据中国的具体情况进行了调整。任何特定国家的法学家在这方面都无法帮助中国法官，因为不同国家所遵循的西方法律观念之间的差异，与任何西方法律观念与中国法律观念之间的差异一样大。只有那些既精通西方法律体系又精通中国传统法律体系的中国法学家，才能在新旧观念之间做出调整。至于会审公廨双重法官制度的弊端，只需引用英国出庭大律师、前会审公廨律师公会成员拉特（Latter）先生在《法律季评》（Law Quarterly Review）中的话即可：

“本法院（会审公廨）的诉讼程序往往演变为陪审判员与谳员之间的纯粹争吵，各自为其本国臣民的利益辩护。有时法院在严重分歧中休庭。有时，法院厌倦了这种内部争斗，便将球踢回给诉讼当事人，让他们自行解决……”

备忘录还赞扬了西方律师在维持法院标准方面所发挥的作用。尽管对这些律师的正直和能力表示敬意，但不可否认，在纯民事案件中，由于这些律师说着不同的语言，主张不同的法律体系，并收取不受监管的费用，浪费了大量时间并造成了诸多不便。通过掮客招揽业务的丑恶做法已被提及。笔者不打算讨论在法院移交后将其排除在外的问题，因为负责此项任务的人员自会找到解决办法。但有一点必须注意。会审公廨根据领事团的指示，在批准人员加入律师公会方面一直非常宽松。我们的《律师章程》规定了加入中国律师公会所需的明确资格。但不常发生的情况是，远未达到这些资格的人，仅凭一两名律师的推荐，就被允许在会审公廨执业。这些人往往只是外国律师的翻译，几乎没受过通识教育，更不用说具备法律知识了。为了提高会审公廨律师公会的道德和智力标准，当局今后务必确保，凡不符合司法部颁布的《律师章程》资格者，一律不得准入。

最后，笔者谨希望，那些肩负着就会审公廨问题进行谈判这一艰巨任务的人，能够充分意识到自己的责任，不受“公众运动”的影响，同时也听取符合公共福利愿望的建议。

感谢贵刊提供版面。
此致，
梁永礼（LIANG YUENG-LI，音译）
上海，1926年7月15日。

'CONSULAR BODY'S PLAN
MENACES RIGHTS OF
ALL FOREIGNERS HERE'

American Bar Association Asserts That Terrible
Conditions Once Prevailing Might Return In Case
Mixed Court Is Given Into Chinese Control
Without Safeguards—Resume Negotiations.

Extraterritorial Rights of all foreigners in Shang-
hai are threatened by the proposed action of the Con-
sular Body, is the assertion of the American Far Eastern
Bar Association in a manifesto which is as follows:
"On the 2nd of July, 1926, the local Chinese authori-
ties made a proposal to the Consular Body for the
rendition of the Mixed Court. The Consular Body com-
mittee drew up a counter proposal which it is reported
has been submitted to the Chinese authorities by the
Consular Body.
"An examination of the Consular Body's counter
proposal will show that an attempt is being made by the
Chinese to strike at the very heart of extraterritorial
rights.
"Article 3 of the Consular Body proposal reads as
follows: —
"In criminal cases which directly affect the
peace and order of the International Settlement,
including contraventions of and Regulations and
Bye-laws of the Shanghai Municipal Council, and
in all criminal cases in which the accused is in the
employ of a foreigner having extraterritorial
rights, the Senior Consul may appoint a deputy to
sit with the Judge to watch the proceeding. The
concurrence of the deputy shall not be necessary
for the validity of the judgment, though he shall
have the right to record objections: he shall
not, however, put any questions to the witness or
prisoners without the consent of the Judge."

This means that the Senior Con-
sul's deputy (assessor) can take
no part in Mixed Court proceed-
ings; he cannot ask the witnesses
or prisoners any questions; his
concurrence is not necessary for the
validity of the judgment. The en-
tire power and authority is in the
hands of a Chinese Judge. As this
Court will function as a Chinese
Court, using such Chinese law and
procedure as is available and deem-
ed in force by the Chinese Judge,
foreign lawyers will not be allow-
ed to appear in the Court or to
prosecute and defend cases in the
Court. It will be necessary for for-
eigners to employ Chinese lawyers
to appear for them.

EXPLAINS PROCEDURE
"Under Chinese procedure a
Chinese lawyer has no right to
examine or cross-examine wit-
nesses. This is done by the Chinese
Judge. A Chinese lawyer is allow-
ed to prepare the pleadings, i.e., the
petition or answer and argue the
case and that is all.
"In accordance with the Consu-
lar Body's proposal (which the
Consular Body have agreed to, as
they propose it to the Chinese),
Art. 4:
"All summonses, warrants
and orders of the Court shall
be valid after they have been
signed by a (Chinese) Judge.
All such summonses, warrants
and orders shall be numbered
for record by the Registrar be-
fore service. When the sum-
mons, warrant or order is to
be executed on premises oc-
cupied by a foreigner having
extraterritorial rights, the
Consul concerned shall on pre-
sentation affix his counter-
signature without delay."
"This means that a Chinese judge
can issue Search Warrant to search
the premises of an American citi-
zen or British subject, and the
American or British Consul agrees
and contracts to counter-sign this
Search Warrant or other order
without delay."
The Consul has no discretion in
the matter and reserves no right
upon which he can base a refusal.
This applies to all summonses, all
warrants and all orders issued by
the Chinese Judge under Chinese
law and procedure.
"Just what Chinese law and pro-
cedure is today, no one knows;
China has no Constitution, no
Code of Laws, no established
Common Law. The deci-
sion of a magistrate depends in
every case upon his personal opin-
ion and whim; it also often depends
upon influence brought to bear
upon him by superior officials,
guilds, friends and interested par-
ties to litigation.
When this proposed agreement
is signed the Chinese may be de-
pended upon to demand the exact
and specific carrying out of all the
terms and conditions in this agree-
ment.

MEANS AGREEMENT
"As by offering the above coun-
ter-proposal the Consular Body
have agreed to sacrifice the
Treaty rights of foreign business
men in Shanghai to the desires of
ambitious Chinese; Chinese am-
bitions for more power and
authority.
"This power and authority is
being given to the Chinese and
this arrangement has been agreed
to by the Consular Body without
consulting the business men of
this Settlement all of whom are
vitally interested. This not only
affects foreigners with Extrater-
ritorial rights but particularly
Germans, Russians and others
will be subject to the tender
mercies of a Chinese Judge, Chin-
ese law and Chinese procedure.
"Respectable Chinese in the
Settlement will also be without
the protection they now have
under the jurisdiction of the In-
ternational Mixed Court. Most of
the wealthy Chinese who reside in
the Settlement, do so for safety.
They come voluntarily within the
jurisdiction of the International
Mixed Court so that their per-
sonal rights and property will be
safe and not subject to the de-
mands of unscrupulous military
leaders and other corrupt officials.
"It must be obvious that hand-
ing back the Mixed Court under
these conditions will seriously
and adversely affect all foreign and
Chinese business in Shanghai and
this in turn will result in further
business depression and deprecia-
tion of land values.

“领事团计划
威胁在此所有外国人之权利”

美国律师协会断言，若会审公廨在无保障措施的情况下移交中方控制，曾经盛行的恶劣状况可能会卷土重来——应恢复谈判。

美国远东律师协会在一份宣言中断言，领事团拟采取的行动威胁到上海所有外国人的治外法权，该宣言内容如下：
“1926年7月2日，中国地方当局向领事团提出移交会审公廨的建议。领事团委员会起草了一份反建议，据悉已由领事团提交给中国当局。
“审查领事团的反建议就会发现，中方正试图打击治外法权的核心。
“领事团提案第三条规定如下：—
“在直接影响公共租界和平与秩序的刑事案件中，包括违反工部局规章及附则的案件，以及所有被告受雇于享有治外法权的外国人的刑事案件，首席领事可指派一名副手（陪审员）与法官同席以监视诉讼程序。该副手的同意并非判决生效的必要条件，尽管他有权记录异议；但是，未经法官同意，他不得向证人或囚犯提出任何问题。”

这意味着首席领事的副手（陪审员）不能参与会审公廨的诉讼程序；他不能向证人或囚犯询问任何问题；他的同意对于判决的有效性并非必要。全部权力和权威掌握在中国法官手中。由于该法庭将作为中国法庭运作，使用中国法官认为可用且有效的中国法律和程序，外国律师将不被允许出庭或在法庭上起诉和辩护案件。外国人必须聘请中国律师代表他们出庭。

解释程序
“根据中国程序，中国律师无权讯问或交叉讯问证人。这由中国法官进行。中国律师仅被允许准备诉状，即请愿书或答辩状，并就案件进行辩论，仅此而已。
“根据领事团的提案（领事团已同意该提案，因为他们将其提议给中方），第四条规定：
“所有传票、逮捕令及法庭命令经（中国）法官签署后即有效。所有此类传票、逮捕令和命令在送达前应由书记官编号存档。当传票、逮捕令或命令需要在享有治外法权的外国人所占用的处所执行时，有关领事应在出示后立即加签副署。”
“这意味着中国法官可以签发搜查令，搜查美国公民或英国臣民的处所，而美国或英国领事同意并承诺立即对该搜查令或其他命令加签副署。”
领事在此事上没有裁量权，也没有保留任何可以作为拒绝依据的权利。这适用于中国法官根据中国法律和程序发出的所有传票、所有逮捕令和所有命令。
“如今究竟什么是中国法律和程序，无人知晓；中国没有宪法，没有法典，没有既定的普通法。治安官的裁决在每一起案件中都取决于其个人意见和一时兴起；这也往往取决于上级官员、行会、朋友和诉讼利害关系人对其施加的影响。
一旦签署这项拟议协议，就可以指望中方要求确切且具体地执行本协议中的所有条款和条件。

意味着协议
“正如通过提出上述反建议，领事团已同意牺牲上海外国商人的条约权利，以满足野心勃勃的中方人士对更多权力和权威的渴望。
“这种权力和权威正被赋予中方，且这一安排已得到领事团的同意，而未咨询本租界内所有切身利益相关的商人。这不仅影响享有治外法权的外国人，特别是德国人、俄国人和其他人将受制于中国法官、中国法律和中国程序的摆布。
“租界内的体面中国人也将失去他们在国际会审公廨管辖下目前拥有的保护。大多数居住在租界的富裕中国人，是为了安全才住在这里。他们自愿接受国际会审公廨的管辖，以便其人身权利和财产得到保障，不受无良军事领袖和其他腐败官员的勒索。
“显而易见，在这些条件下交还会审公廨将严重且不利地影响上海的所有外国和中国商业，而这反过来又将导致进一步的商业萧条和土地价值贬值。

"The political situation through-
out China indicates to the man of
ordinary intelligence the reliance
that can be placed upon Chinese
military leaders and Chinese
Courts. The scandalous Osterm-
off case, where a responsible, re-
putable Russian was kept a pris-
oner in a filthy jail for months
without charges being filed against
him or his case being heard; the
case of the German at Hankow
sent to jail for 15 years charged
with murder of a Chinese child,
who fell down and hit its head on
a stone road and died, but who
was not struck by the German;
the case of the Russian launch
Captain now in jail in Newchwang
on a charge of murder, his launch
having collided with a Chinese
boat; and hundreds of other out-
rageous cases indicate what can
be and is done by Chinese Judges
under Chinese law and procedure.
Such occurrences will arise in
Shanghai unless the return of the
International Mixed Court is sub-
ject to the adequate safeguards
under the control of the Shanghai
Municipal Council as it is at the
present time.

REVIEWS HISTORY
"In 1911 when Shanghai went
over to the Revolutionaries the
Chief Magistrate of the Mixed
Court absconded with some $30,-
000 of the Court funds. The
Revolution left Shanghai without
any recognized authority and the
Consular Body took control of the
Mixed Court in all cases, civil and
criminal.
"Some of the abuses of the
Court prior to the Revolution in
1911 were:
"1st. Judgments in foreign
civil cases were most difficult to
enforce.
"2nd. Chinese officials of the
Court, including runners, Magis-
trates and Taotais, extorted bribes
and acted accordingly;
"3rd. The secretary of the
Court, prior to the Revolution,
kept an office on Koochow Road
for the purpose of arranging
bribes for the Magistrates and
other officials. He was murdered
for receiving bribes from both
parties to an action.
"4th. In one case a Chinese,
who was illegally arrested in the
Settlement by runners of the
Native City Magistrate sought the
protection of the Settlement
Authorities and for this was ham-
bood until the bones of his legs
were exposed;
"5th. Mixed Court orders,
placed in the hands of native
runners, were used for the pur-
pose of extortion;
"6th. Sentences of imprison-
ment were disregarded, some pris-
oners being released long before
their terms expired, others being
detained for months after their
terms expired;
"7th. Guarantors of no sub-
stance were accepted by the Ma-
gistrates to guarantee enormous
obligations;
"8th. Paupers and coolies were
paid to substitute for influential
persons detained in civil actions;
"9th. Constant interference on
the part of higher officials, guilds
and individuals with the decisions
of the Court was customary.

Since the Revolution in 1911
the administration of the Court
has steadily improved and an un-
precedented growth in Shanghai
land values, vested interests and
population has taken place. The
large influx of Chinese from the
interior indicates that they come
to this Settlement seeking the
protection of a more orderly and
better governed locality where
they know that they will not be
arbitrarily deprived of their
rights or property.

IMPROVEMENTS STATED
"Some of the improvements in
the Court since 1911 are:
"1st. Civil and criminal pro-
cesses are handled by the Muni-
cipal Police under the direction of
the Consular Body;
"2nd. The corrupt runners
have been eliminated;
"3rd. The civil cells and
female ward are properly con-
trolled by the Consular Body
through the Municipal Police;
"4th. Criminal cases involving
punishment of over five years are
tried in the Mixed Court, doing
away with the abuses consequent
upon the trial of such cases in
the native city;
"5th. Inquests are held in the
Settlement by Assessors and Ma-
gistrates sitting together. There
are no more coroners' verdicts like
that over the body with a crushed
skull, "Died of sickness," the
theory being that only wounds in
the thorax were fatal;
"6th. Interference with the
Court by high Chinese Officials
and commercial bodies has been
largely eliminated;
"7th. The finances of the Court
are honestly controlled and ad-
ministered by the Consular Body
through the Municipal Council;
"8th. Chinese civil cases are
tried by Assessors and Magis-
trates sitting together, the As-
sessors having the balance of
power;
"9th. Extradition of Chinese
from the Settlement to the in-
terior is only allowed upon the
showing of a prima facie case;
"10th. The Magistrates are
now chosen by the Consular Body
and their salaries are regularly
paid, thereby making them less
dependent and less susceptible to
the "charm of silver."
"Under the law as now ad-
ministered in the Mixed Court
both parties are entitled to be
represented by counsel, who may
examine and cross-examine wit-
nesses in their behalf. The deci-
sions of the Court are rendered
only upon evidence produced in
Court.
"The operation of railways in
China; the embezzling and mis-
appropriating of city funds at
Tsingtao; the failure of the Chin-
ese Government to pay legitimate
debts prove the notorious fact
that the Chinese Government can-
not meet its financial obligations,
nor do we believe that the Chin-
ese Government would pay the
expenses of such a Court. The
expenses of the Mixed Court aver-
age about Tls. 140,000 per annum.
This at the present time is being
paid by the Shanghai Municipal
Council. With no check or safe-
guards the temptation to use the

funds of the Court illegally would
be too great,, as proved by past
experience.
"The Washington Conference
provided for a Commission to in-
vestigate the Judicial System and
the methods of judicial adminis-
tration of China with a view to
the abolition of extraterritoriality.
The rendition of the Mixed Court
should await the report of this
Commission.

“整个中国的政治局势向具有普通智力的人表明，对中国军事领袖和中国法院可以寄予何种信赖。臭名昭著的奥斯特莫夫（Ostermoff）案，其中一名负责任、有声望的俄国人在未对他提出指控或审理其案件的情况下，被关押在肮脏的监狱中数月；汉口一名德国人被控谋杀一名中国儿童而入狱15年，该儿童跌倒头部撞到石头路面身亡，但并未受到该德国人的殴打；现在营口因谋杀罪入狱的一名俄国汽艇船长案，其汽艇与一艘中国船只相撞；以及其他数百起骇人听闻的案件，表明了中国法官在中国法律和程序下能够做且正在做的事情。
除非像目前那样，在国际会审公廨的归还受到工部局控制下的充分保障措施制约，否则此类事件将在上海发生。

回顾历史
“1911年上海转向革命党人时，会审公廨的首席治安官携约3万美元的法庭资金潜逃。革命使上海没有任何公认的权威，领事团接管了会审公廨的所有民事和刑事案件。
“1911年革命前法庭的一些弊端是：
“1. 外国民事案件的判决最难执行。
“2. 法庭的中国官员，包括差役、治安官和道台，敲诈贿赂并据此行事；
“3. 革命前，法庭秘书在顾家宅路（Koochow Road）设有一个办事处，目的是为治安官和其他官员安排贿赂。他因收受诉讼双方的贿赂而被谋杀。
“4. 在一桩案件中，一名中国人在租界内被华界治安官的差役非法逮捕，他寻求租界当局的保护，为此遭到毒打直至腿骨外露；
“5. 交给华籍差役执行的会审公廨命令被用于敲诈目的；
“6. 监禁刑期被无视，一些囚犯在刑期届满前很久就被释放，另一些则在刑期届满后被拘禁数月；
“7. 治安官接受毫无资力的担保人担保巨额债务；
“8. 支付贫民和苦力代替在民事诉讼中被拘留的有影响力的人物；
“9. 高级官员、行会和个人不断干涉法庭裁决已成为惯例。

自1911年革命以来，法庭的管理稳步改善，上海的土地价值、既得利益和人口出现了前所未有的增长。大量来自内地的中国人涌入，表明他们来到本租界是寻求一个更有秩序、治理更好的地方的保护，在那里他们知道不会任意被剥夺权利或财产。

陈述改进情况
“自1911年以来，法庭的一些改进包括：
“1. 民事和刑事诉讼程序由领事团指导下的工部局警务处处理；
“2. 腐败的差役已被清除；
“3. 民事牢房和女监区由领事团通过工部局警务处进行适当控制；
“4. 涉及五年以上刑罚的刑事案件在会审公廨审理，从而消除了在华界审理此类案件随之而来的弊端；
“5. 验尸调查在租界内由陪审员和治安官共同主持进行。不再有类似头骨粉碎的尸体被裁定为‘病死’这样的验尸官裁决，其理论是只有胸部的伤口才是致命的；
“6. 中国高官和商业团体对法庭的干涉已基本消除；
“7. 法庭的财务由领事团通过工部局诚实控制和管理；
“8. 中国民事案件由陪审员和治安官共同审理，陪审员拥有平衡权力；
“9. 只有在出示表面证据确凿的案件后，才允许将中国人从租界引渡至内地；
“10. 治安官现在由领事团选定，他们的薪水定期发放，从而使他们较少依赖他人，较不易受‘银子的魅力’（贿赂）的影响。
“根据目前在会审公廨实施的法律，双方均有权由律师代表，律师可以代表他们讯问和交叉讯问证人。法庭的裁决仅依据法庭上提出的证据作出。
“中国铁路的运营；青岛城市资金的贪污和挪用；中国政府未能偿还合法债务，这些证明了众所周知的事实，即中国政府无法履行其财政义务，我们也不相信中国政府会支付此类法庭的费用。会审公廨的费用平均每年约为规元14万两。目前这笔费用由上海工部局支付。若无检查或保障措施，非法使用法庭资金的诱惑将太大，过去的经验已证明了这一点。
“华盛顿会议规定成立一个委员会，调查中国的司法制度和司法行政方法，以期废除治外法权。会审公廨的移交通常应等待该委员会的报告。
“远东美国律师协会”

Lawyers Astounded At
Mixed Court Agreement

The committee, appointed by the legal fraternity practicing in Shanghai, to deal with the question of the Mixed Court issue met last night to discuss points in connection with the situation.

At the meeting it was decided that the published agreement is of such an astounding nature that the delegation of five will start for Peking unless the document is actually rescinded in Shanghai.

The opinion was held that all the local organisations would join in the protest with the lawyers except the British Chamber of Commerce, which from previous promises, has agreed to the principles of rendition of the court.

It was presumed, however, that having had an opportunity to read the full text of the agreement the British Chamber of Commerce might be just as anxious as any other foreign element to realise the effects of such an agreement and join in the general protest.

The committee also decided to write the Consular Body in order to secure an interview during which the document might be discussed.

In order fully to explain the meaning of the agreement, which up to the moment has only been signed by the representatives of the Chinese Authorities, and to give the public an opportunity of fully realising what might happen should the rendition of the Mixed Court become an actuality the Far Eastern American Bar Association has published the following memorandum:

Rendition Of The
International Mixed
Court At Shanghai

In view of the imminent rendition of the Mixed Court the undersigned consider it appropriate to offer this memorandum in the hope that the advantages, secured after fifty-five years of attempted reform, be not lost.

Prior to 1864 most cases against Chinese of the International Settlement were sent to the City Magistrate or Taotai for trial. This proved intolerable and the International Mixed Court was established in 1869. The British-Chinese Agreement of 1876 (Section

2, Article 2 and 3) states that the Chinese Government has established a Mixed Court at Shanghai. At that time it was noted that the Magistrate of the Mixed Court "Constantly fails to enforce his judgments" and reforms were contemplated.

The powers of Assessors were persuasive up to 1905 when the Municipal Police were first used in the criminal branch of the Court. From 1905 to 1911 the Assessors gradually assumed the balance of power over the Chinese Magistrates in criminal cases. When Shanghai went over to the Revolutionaries the Chief Magistrate absconded with some $60,000.00 of the Court funds. The Revolution left Shanghai without any recognized authority and the Consular Body, as a matter of expediency, assumed entire control over the Mixed Court in all cases, civil and criminal.

Some of the abuses of the Court prior to the Revolution in 1911 were:—

1st. Judgments in foreign civil cases were most difficult to enforce;

2nd. Chinese officials of the Court, including runners, Magistrates and Taotais, extorted bribes and acted accordingly;

3rd. The secretary of the Court, prior to the Revolution, kept an office on Foochow Road for the purpose of arranging bribes for the Magistrates and other officials. He was murdered for receiving bribes from both parties to an action;

4th. In one case a Chinese, who was illegally arrested in the Settlement by runners of the Native City Magistrate, sought the protection of the Settlement Authorities and for this was bambooed until the bones of his legs were exposed;

5th. Mixed Court orders, placed in the hands of native runners, were used for the purpose of extortion;

6th. Sentences of imprisonment were disregarded, some prisoners being released long before their terms expired, others being detained for months after their terms expired;

7th. Guarantors of no substance were accepted by the Magistrates to guarantee enormous obligations;

8th. Paupers and coolies were used to substitute for influential persons detained in civil actions;

9th. Constant interference on the part of higher officials, guides and individuals with the decisions of the Court was customary.

Since the Revolution in 1911 the administration of the Court has steadily improved and an unprecedented growth in Shanghai land values, vested interests and population has taken place. The large influx of Chinese from the interior indicates that they come to the Settlement seeking the protection of a more orderly and better governed locality where they know that they will not be arbitrarily deprived of their rights or property.

Some of the improvements in the Court since 1911 are:—1st. Civil and criminal processes are handled by the Municipal Police under the direction of the Consular Body.

2nd. The corrupt runners have been eliminated;

3rd. The civil cells and female ward are properly controlled by the Consular Body through the Municipal Police.

4th. Criminal cases involving punishment of over five years are tried in the Mixed Court, doing away with the abuses consequent upon the trial of such cases in the native city.

5th. Inquests are held in the Settlement by Assessors and Magistrates sitting together. There are no more corner verdicts like that over a body with a crushed skull "Died of sickness," the theory being that only wounds in the thorax were fatal.

6th. Interference with the Court by high Chinese Officials and commercial bodies has been largely eliminated.

7th. The finances of the Court are honestly controlled and administered by the Consular Body through the Municipal Council;

8th. Chinese civil cases are tried by Assessors and Magistrates sitting together, the Assessors having the balance of power;

9th. Extradition of Chinese from the Settlement to the interior is only allowed upon the showing of prima facie cases;

10th. The Magistrates are now chosen by the Consular Body and their salaries are regularly paid, thereby making them less dependent and less susceptible to the charm of silver.

Under the law as now administered in the Mixed Court both parties are entitled to be represented by counsel who may examine and cross-examine witnesses in their behalf. 律师界对会审公廨协定感到震惊

由在上海执业的法律界人士组成的、负责处理会审公廨问题的委员会昨晚召开会议，讨论与当前局势相关的要点。

会议决定，鉴于已公布的协定性质令人震惊，除非该文件在上海被实际撤销，否则五人代表团将启程前往北京。

与会者认为，除英国商会外，所有本地组织都将与律师界一起提出抗议；英国商会基于先前的承诺，已同意交还会审公廨的原则。

然而，据推测，英国商会在有机会阅读协定的全文后，可能会像其他外籍人士一样，急于认识到此类协定的影响，并加入普遍的抗议行列。

委员会还决定致函领事团，以求获得一次会晤机会，在此期间可以讨论该文件。

为了充分解释该协定的含义（截至目前，该协定仅由中国当局代表签署），并使公众充分认识到如果会审公廨的移交成为现实可能会发生什么情况，远东美国律师协会发布了以下备忘录：

上海
国际会审公廨
之移交

鉴于会审公廨即将移交，签署人认为提出本备忘录是适当的，希望经过五十五年改革尝试所获得的利益不致丧失。

1864年以前，公共租界内针对中国人的大多数案件都被送交上海县知事或道台审理。这被证明是难以忍受的，于是国际会审公廨于1869年成立。1876年的《中英协定》（第二节，第二和第三条）规定，中国政府在上海设立了一个会审公廨。当时有人指出，会审公廨的谳员“经常无法执行其判决”，因此人们考虑进行改革。

陪审官（Assessors）的影响力一直持续到1905年，当时工部局警务处首次被用于该法庭的刑事部门。从1905年到1911年，陪审官在刑事案件中逐渐掌握了相对于中国谳员的权力平衡。当上海转向革命党人时，首席谳员携约60,000.00美元的法庭资金潜逃。革命使上海没有任何公认的权威，领事团出于权宜之计，接管了会审公廨在所有民事和刑事案件中的全部控制权。

1911年革命前，法庭的一些弊端如下：—

第一，外国民事案件的判决最难执行；

第二，法庭的中国官员，包括差役、谳员和道台，勒索贿赂并据此行事；

第三，革命前，法庭秘书在福州路设有一个办事处，目的是为谳员和其他官员安排贿赂。他因收受诉讼双方的贿赂而被谋杀；

第四，在一个案件中，一名中国人在租界内被华界县知事的差役非法逮捕，他寻求租界当局的保护，为此遭到竹杖责打，直至腿骨外露；

第五，落入华籍差役手中的会审公廨命令被用于勒索目的；

第六，监禁判决被无视，一些囚犯在刑期届满前很久就被释放，另一些则在刑期届满后被拘押数月；

第七，谳员接受毫无资产的保证人来担保巨额债务；

第八，使用贫民和苦力代替在民事诉讼中被拘留的有影响力的人物；

第九，高级官员、向导和个人不断干涉法庭判决已成为惯例。

自1911年革命以来，法庭的管理稳步改善，上海的土地价值、既得利益和人口出现了前所未有的增长。大量来自内地的中国人涌入，表明他们来到租界是为了寻求一个更有秩序、治理更好的地方的保护，因为他们知道在那里他们的权利或财产不会被任意剥夺。

自1911年以来，法庭的一些改进包括：—第一，民事和刑事诉讼程序由工部局警务处在领事团的指导下处理。

第二，腐败的差役已被清除；

第三，民事拘留室和女监由领事团通过工部局警务处进行适当控制。

第四，涉及五年以上刑罚的刑事案件在会审公廨审理，从而消除了此类案件在华界审理所带来的弊端。

第五，验尸由陪审官和谳员共同主持在租界内进行。再也不会有像对着颅骨粉碎的尸体作出“病死”判决那样的荒谬结论了，其理论依据是只有胸部的伤口才是致命的。

第六，中国高官和商业团体对法庭的干涉已基本消除。

第七，法庭的财务由领事团通过工部局诚实控制和管理；

第八，中国民事案件由陪审官和谳员共同审理，陪审官掌握权力平衡；

第九，只有在出示初步证据案件的情况下，才允许将中国人从租界引渡至内地；

第十，谳员现在由领事团选定，他们的薪水定期支付，从而使他们较少依赖他人，也不太容易受到金钱的诱惑。

根据目前在会审公廨实施的法律，双方均有权由律师代理，律师可以代表他们讯问和交叉讯问证人。法庭的判决仅依据庭上提出的证据作出。根据现行的中国司法程序，虽然当事人有权由律师代理，但律师无权讯问或交叉讯问证人。中国法官可以，在

their own initiative, secretly investigate the evidence. (Articles 463, 642, 675 and 710 of the Chinese Code of Civil Procedure.) In a recent case tried in the local Chinese District Court at Shanghai, the Court held that it would not hear the evidence of a certain material witness because the Magistrate himself had investigated the evidence, and therefore that proof was unnecessary. (See THE CHINA PRESS of December 9, 1922, entitled "Magistrate In Turns Detective in Tong Trial".) Such methods would undoubtedly be adopted in the Mixed Court if it were returned unconditionally. The handing over of the Mixed Court without adequate safeguards would probably mean a revival of the old abuses, corruption, bribery and chicanery that existed in the Court prior to 1911.

RECOMMENDATIONS
To safeguard the reforms and improvements of 55 years of effort and to further continue those improvements we urge that the rendition be contingent upon the following conditions:—

FOREIGN JUDGES.
Most of the recently enacted statutory laws in China are modeled after those of Western Countries and Chinese Judges cannot be expected to administer Western conceptions of law without guidance. If the Chinese civil cases were now to be tried by a Chinese Magistrate sitting alone, we would expect the old abuses and corruption to reappear.
We, therefore, suggest that the handing back of the Mixed Court be conditional upon the appointment of an equal number of Western and Chinese Judges of high standing and integrity, all appointed and paid by the Chinese Government.

APPEAL COURT
From the Local District Court at Shanghai there lies an appeal to the High Court at Soochow. An appeal from the International Mixed Court to the High Court at Soochow does not give adequate consideration to the importance of Shanghai as compared with Soochow. The Appeal Court should be located in the Foreign Settlement at Shanghai, and a further appeal might be had to the Supreme Court at Peking. Such an Appeal Court at Shanghai could not properly function over the Mixed Court without a similar inclusion of foreign Judges.
It is accordingly recommended that foreign Judges, understanding the Chinese language, customs and laws, be appointed and paid by the Chinese Government for this Judicial Branch. The Mixed Court with its Trial and Appellate Divisions could then easily become a model Court for all China.

FOREIGN LAWYERS
It is generally conceded that the appearance of Western lawyers in the Mixed Court has done much to obtain that security in the International Settlement which has made possible Shanghai's greatest growth in its history. The development of the law and procedure depends largely upon the activities of the Bar. If the Chinese civil cases are to be tried by Chinese Magistrates sitting alone, Western lawyers would disappear from the Court. All of the high traditions of the Western Bars would be lost to the Court, and the old methods would be substituted. Lawyers are officers of the Court and the standing of the Court depends upon the character, ability and integrity of the lawyers that appear before it. Before 1911 there were no Chinese lawyers. It has been possible for the Chinese to have built up a Bar of high standards within the space of thirteen years, especially as prior to the Revolution petition writers and legal advisors were a low and discredited class and were considered a menace to the administration of justice.
Western lawyers have a substantial vested interest in their practice in the International Mixed Court. This practice has been developed by hard work, training, ability, integrity and a desire to see that justice is impartially and fairly administered. The deprivation of the right of foreign lawyers, either actively or impliedly, to appear before the International Mixed Court would hinder the administration of justice.

FOREIGN REGISTRAR
The last Magistrate of the Mixed Court before the Revolution embezzled $60,000.00 from the Court funds. Magistrate Mei Yi-kuo, Chief of the Chinese District Court at Shanghai, also absconded in 1923 after having embezzled over $40,000.00 of Court funds. During the administration of the Consular Body over the Court, litigants have felt secure in depositing funds with the Court. Should the Court be turned over to the Chinese Government without the suggested supervision, the Court funds would not be safe.
We, therefore, recommend that the finances of the Court be put in charge of a foreign Registrar appointed by the Chinese Government with the approval of the Consular Body and that such foreign representative be bonded to guarantee the faithful performance of his duties.

COURT EXPENSES
It is a notorious fact that the Chinese Government cannot meet its financial obligations, nor do we believe that the Chinese Government would pay the expenses of such a Court. The expenses of the Mixed Court average about Tls. 140,000.00 per annum. This at the present time is being paid by the Shanghai Municipal Council. With no check or safeguard the temptation to use the funds of the Court illegally would be too great, as proved by past experience. The Chinese Government should be required to deposit with the Shanghai Municipal Council a sufficient sum, yearly, in advance to cover the cost of operating the Mixed Court.

MIXED COURT PROCESSES
Chinese runners, used by the Native Courts to serve processes, are corrupt. For a few dollars they will falsely report that a defendant has absconded or swear out false processes. If the Mixed Court is returned it should be on the condition that processes be served by the Shanghai Municipal Police under the direction of the Consular Body.

MIXED COURT JUDGMENTS
Interior Courts must enforce the judgments of the Mixed Court and vice versa. There must be mutual co-operation between the Mixed Court and all Chinese Courts. The handing over of the Mixed Court should be conditional upon its orders, judgments and warrants being carried out and executed by Interior Courts.

ALL PLEADINGS AND JUDGMENTS TO BE IN CHINESE AND ENGLISH
In order to achieve the high standard proposed, all pleadings, wherever possible, should be in the English and Chinese languages. Cases should also be tried in both English and Chinese. Complete Court records should be kept in both English and Chinese for use on appeal, including a transcript of the evidence. We advise the use of the English language during this transitory period as an essential to the best interpretation and administration of the New Chinese Codes which are based on Western laws.

RENDITION TO BE POSTPONED UNTIL THE REPORT OF THE COMMISSION TO INVESTIGATE EXTRATERRITORIALITY.
The Washington Conference provided for a Commission to investigate the Judicial System and the methods of judicial administration of China with a view to the abolition of extraterritoriality. The rendition of the Mixed Court should await the report of this Commission.

Respectfully Submitted,
Far Eastern American
Bar Association.

建议

为保障55年来努力取得的改革与进步，并进一步推动这些改进，我们恳请将交还事宜取决于以下条件：—

外籍法官。
中国近期颁布的成文法大多仿效西方国家法律，若不加指导，不能指望中国法官能够施行西方法律理念。如果中国民事案件现在由一名中国推事单独审理，我们预计旧的弊端和腐败将会重现。
因此，我们建议，交还会审公廨应以任命同等数量的德高望重且正直的外籍和中国法官为条件，所有法官均由中国政府任命并支付薪俸。

上诉法院
从上海地方地方法院可上诉至苏州高等法院。从国际会审公廨上诉至苏州高等法院，未能充分考虑上海相较于苏州的重要性。上诉法院应设在上海外国租界内，并可进一步上诉至北京最高法院。如果没有同样纳入外籍法官，设在上海的此类上诉法院无法在会审公廨之上正常运作。
因此，建议由中国政府任命并支付薪俸，为该司法部门配备通晓中文、习俗和法律的外籍法官。如此一来，设有审判庭和上诉庭的会审公廨便可轻易成为全中国的模范法院。

外籍律师
人们普遍承认，外籍律师出现在会审公廨，极大地促成了国际租界的安全，从而使上海取得了历史上最大的发展。法律及程序的发展很大程度上取决于律师界的活跃程度。如果中国民事案件由中国推事单独审理，外籍律师将从法院消失。法院将失去西方律师界的所有高尚传统，而代之以旧式方法。律师是法院的职员，法院的地位取决于出庭律师的品格、能力和正直程度。1911年以前没有中国律师。中国人在十三年内建立起高标准的律师界是可能的，尤其是在革命之前，代书人和法律顾问是一个地位低下且声名狼藉的阶层，被视为对司法行政的威胁。
外籍律师在国际会审公廨的执业拥有实质性的既得利益。这种执业是通过努力工作、培训、能力、正直以及希望看到公正无私地实施正义而发展起来的。剥夺外籍律师在国际会审公廨出庭的权利，无论是明示还是暗示，都将阻碍司法的实施。

外籍书记官。
革命前会审公廨的最后一任推事从法院资金中侵吞了60,000.00美元。上海中国地方法院院长梅义国（Mei Yi-kuo，音译）推事也在1923年卷款潜逃，此前他侵吞了超过40,000.00美元的法院资金。在领事团管理法院期间，诉讼当事人对向法院存款感到安全。如果法院在没有建议的监督情况下移交给中国政府，法院资金将不安全。
因此，我们建议法院财务由一名外籍书记官负责，该书记官由中国政府任命并经领事团批准，且该外籍代表需提供保证金以保证其忠实履行职责。

法院费用。
中国政府无法履行其财政义务是一个众所周知的事实，我们也不相信中国政府会支付此类法院的费用。会审公廨的平均费用约为每年规元140,000.00两。目前这笔费用由上海工部局支付。正如过去的经验所证明，如果没有检查或保障，非法使用法院资金的诱惑将太大。应要求中国政府每年预先向上海工部局存入足够数额的款项，以支付会审公廨的运营成本。

会审公廨传票送达
中国地方法院使用的中国差役在送达传票方面存在腐败行为。只需几美元，他们就会虚假报告被告已潜逃，或出具虚假传票。如果交还会审公廨，应以传票由领事团指导下的上海公共租界工部局警务处送达为条件。

会审公廨判决
内地法院必须执行会审公廨的判决，反之亦然。会审公廨与所有中国法院之间必须有相互合作。交还会审公廨应以其命令、判决和令状由内地法院执行和实施为条件。

所有诉状和判决书均使用中文和英文
为了达到所提议的高标准，所有诉状在可能的情况下均应使用英文和中文。案件也应使用英文和中文进行审理。完整的法院记录应同时保留英文和中文版本，以供上诉时使用，包括证据誊本。我们建议在这一过渡时期使用英文，这对于基于西方法律的新中国法典的最佳解释和实施至关重要。

在治外法权调查委员会报告出炉前推迟交还。
华盛顿会议规定设立一个委员会，调查中国的司法制度及司法行政方法，以期废除治外法权。会审公廨的交还应等待该委员会的报告。

此致，
远东美国律师协会
